3. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that on an application under section 12(6) read with 57 Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (herein after referred to as Ain) filed by the respondent No. 2, who is the judgment debtor No. 1, in Artha Rin Jari Mamla No. 51 of 2010 the decreetal amount was refixed at Taka 5,77,22,000 instead of Taka 26,04,14,261.70 with a direction upon the petitioner bank to give opportunity to the judgment debtors i.e. opposite parties Nos. 2 to 4 to pay the said refixed amount within 10(ten) years as per Solenama to be executed with the opposite parties Nos. 2 to 4 and also to withdraw the CIB report after payment of 1% of the 1st installment of the refixed amount as down payment. The impugned order is clearly violative of the relevant provisions of Ain and also relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such, the said order is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 7. It has been also further argued that the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong being the executing court has not been given authority or jurisdiction to refix the decreetal amount and cannot give a direction upon the petitioner bank to enter into an Agreement by way of solenama and withdraw the CIB after 1% down payment on the refixed amount.
